mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite falling FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises faster than the federal funds rate, it may indicate inflationary pressures, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL outpaces FEDFUNDS yet S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with low unemployment (UNRATE) may signal late-cycle economic dynamics, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO and UNRATE indicate late-cycle yet S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strong labor market, which may boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) may indicate reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is below 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with stable retail sales (RSAFS) may indicate economic imbalance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines and RSAFS is stable yet S&P 500 returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) coupled with increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals an early-cycle recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.
